title: Quiz: floating point
prompt: This set covers single and double precision registers, which ones a subroutine has to preserve, conversions between the two formats, and the rules for arithmetic, argument passing, and comparison.

questions.question: What can go wrong when fcvt s0, d0 executes?
options: The program aborts with an alignment fault.
Precision can be lost, because the single-precision destination has fewer fraction bits than the source.
questions.explanation: fcvt s0, d0 converts the double in d0 to a single in s0, rounding to the nearest representable value. A double carries 52 fraction bits and a single carries 23, so the narrowing conversion can round digits away.
questions.hint: Compare the fraction field of a double with the fraction field of a single.

questions.question: In fmadd s0, s1, s2, s3, what value does the destination receive?
questions.explanation: fmadd multiplies the second and third operands and adds the fourth to the product, so s0 gets s3 + s1 * s2. The companion fmsub subtracts the product from the addend instead.
questions.hint: The last operand is the addend, the middle two are the multiplicands.

questions.question: Which floating-point registers must a subroutine preserve across a call, saving and restoring them if it uses them?
questions.explanation: d8 to d15 are the callee-saved floating-point registers, and only their low 64 bits have to survive a call. d0 to d7 carry arguments and results, and d16 to d31 are free for a subroutine to use.
questions.hint: It is the second block of eight registers.

questions.question: How many floating-point arguments can be passed to a subroutine in registers before the rest have to go on the stack?
questions.explanation: The first eight floating-point arguments travel in v0 to v7, read as d0 to d7 for doubles and s0 to s7 for singles. A ninth floating-point argument is passed on the stack.
questions.hint: Count the argument registers from 0 to 7.

questions.question: Where does fcmp d0, d1 leave its result?
options: In the NZCV condition flags, with no register written.
In fpsr, which has to be copied out with mrs before a branch can use it.
questions.explanation: fcmp sets the same NZCV condition flags that cmp sets, so an ordinary conditional branch such as b.eq or b.gt follows it directly. No general-purpose register and no floating-point register is written.
questions.hint: Ask what a conditional branch reads after any compare instruction.
